01 / model

Your model. Your rules.

Entities, facts, variables, and configuration enter through the public facade.

02 / Crate graph

One dependency. Nine crates.

The facade brings the runtime together. Arrows point toward dependencies; the publish rail shows release order.

03 / pipeline

From problem to solution.

Build the runtime, complete required assignments, search, and retain the result. Configured limits remain binding during construction.

04 / runtime

Inside the search loop.

Selectors own candidates. Scoring retains incremental state. Only the selected move transfers by ownership.

05 / ecosystem

A kernel, not a monolith.

Workspace examples use the same facade. CLI, bindings, and visualization tools live in separate repositories.

Read the connections

In the crate graph, arrows point to the dependency. In the solve pipeline, arrows show execution order. Dashed runtime lines show scoring feedback.

Completion is structural

Required assignments must be complete before local search or completed output. If configured termination arrives first, the lifecycle is Failed.

Extend the right layer

Use the domain guide for models and scoring, or the solver guide for phases and search policies.
